description: Increases downtown building height, density, and adaptive reuse options.
Restricts new surface parking on 21st Street and 2nd Avenue.
Expands density bonuses for public benefits like affordable housing.

chips.text: Councillor Ryan Lejbak declared conflict due to owning warehouse district building.
Public engagement showed general support, little opposition to changes.
New density bonus options include bicycle parking and public walkways.

segments.title: B6 Downtown Commercial District Amendments
segments.takeaway: Committee members asked questions about residential setbacks, building code regulations, awnings, and incentives for residential units and grocery stores in the B6 district.

segments.title: MX2 Downtown Warehouse Mixed Use District Amendments
segments.takeaway: Committee members inquired about the "base, middle, top" building articulation requirement and its interpretation for new developments in the MX2 district.

segments.title: Density Bonus Provisions for B6 and MX2
segments.takeaway: Committee members asked about the green roof provision within the density bonusing framework, which is being replaced by a broader certification level.

segments.title: Surface Parking Regulations for Downtown Districts
segments.takeaway: Committee members questioned whether the city was developing financial incentives or penalties to encourage the transition away from surface parking lots.
